correctness.rationale: Conditioning a fixed vertex v to be isolated leaves a uniformly sampled m-edge graph on the B=choose(n-1,2) pairs not touching v. Since H has no isolated vertices, no induced copy contains v; E[X_H|v isolated] follows by prescribed e present and r=choose(h,2)-e absent edges. Dividing by the unconditional induced-count expectation and summing vertex covariances gives R=(n-h)/n (N)_t/(B)_t (B-m)_r/(N-m)_r with N=choose(n,2) and the stated positive normalizing domain. Every factor (B-m-j)/(N-m-j) strictly decreases while positive, and the numerator becomes zero later; hence the one-crossing direction holds. Expanding R at fixed p in (0,1) yields n(R-1)->[2e-h-h(h-2)p]/(1-p). Substituting h=3,e=2 gives M_n=(n-1)(n^3-3n^2+6n+8)/(2(3n^2-3n-4)), with 2<M_n<B. Independently simplified the rational threshold and enumerated all labeled graph outcomes by exact rational counts for wedge counts at n=4,5,6, rather than treating finite enumeration as the all-n proof.

value.rationale: Isolates and induced motifs are fundamental dependent random-graph statistics. The unexpected positive-to-negative covariance transition at fixed edge count, uniform across motif topology at fixed (h,e), is qualitatively unlike the always-negative independent-edge-model covariance. The all-n rational wedge boundary and universal limiting p* are natural dependence-phase invariants, not arbitrary small-instance arithmetic.

final_claim: For G(n,m), the normalized covariance of isolated-vertex count and an induced h-vertex e-edge motif with no isolates and at least one nonedge has the exact hypergeometric ratio R-1 depending only on n,h,e,m; the ratio decreases through at most one positive-to-negative transition. In the bulk the sign threshold is p*=(2e-h)/(h(h-2)) where 2e>h; for P3 an explicit rational finite-n transition M_n tends to density 1/3.
limitations: Requires H no isolated vertices, at least one edge and one missing edge, and positive expectations in e<=m<=min(B,N-r).
The universal coefficient is for fixed h,e and m/N->p strictly between 0 and 1.
